proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent-supplied proof (packing by disjoint balls B(x_i, r/2) and a maximal r-separated family), with the reference set thickening(1, K) in place of K₁ so that the constant does not depend on r.
Notation: Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ = Rn n, B(z,ρ) the open ball, B̄(z,ρ) the closed ball.
1. Constants. Let U := thickening(1, K) = {z : infEdist(z, K) < 1}. Recall z ∈ U iff dist(z, a) < 1 for some a ∈ K (Metric.mem_thickening_iff). Since K is bounded, U is bounded (Bornology.IsBounded.thickening), so Lⁿ(U) < ∞ (Bornology.IsBounded.measure_lt_top). Let A := Lⁿ(U).toReal ≥ 0 and b := Lⁿ(B(0,1)).toReal. Then b > 0, since 0 < Lⁿ(B(0,1)) < ∞ (measure_ball_pos, measure_ball_lt_top). Put C := 2ⁿ·A/b. For all z ∈ ℝⁿ and ρ > 0, Lⁿ(B(z,ρ)) = ofReal(ρⁿ)·Lⁿ(B(0,1)) (Measure.addHaar_ball_of_pos with finrank ℝ ℝⁿ = n; this also holds for n = 0).
Fix r with 0 < r ≤ 1.
2. Packing inequality. Let F ⊆ K be a finite set that is r-separated, i.e. dist(x, x′) > r for all distinct x, x′ ∈ F. The open balls B(x, r/2), x ∈ F, are pairwise disjoint. Indeed, a common point z of B(x, r/2) and B(x′, r/2) would give dist(x, x′) ≤ dist(x, z) + dist(z, x′) < r. Each B(x, r/2) with x ∈ K lies in U, because every z in it has dist(z, x) < r/2 < 1. By finite additivity (measure_biUnion_finset) and monotonicity, card(F)·ofReal((r/2)ⁿ)·Lⁿ(B(0,1)) = Σ_{x∈F} Lⁿ(B(x, r/2)) = Lⁿ(⋃_{x∈F} B(x, r/2)) ≤ Lⁿ(U). All quantities are finite, so applying toReal gives card(F)·((r/2)ⁿ·b) ≤ A.
3. A maximal separated set. Note (r/2)ⁿ·b > 0, and let N := ⌊A/((r/2)ⁿ·b)⌋₊ ∈ ℕ. For c ∈ ℕ let P(c) be the statement: "there is a finite r-separated F ⊆ K with card(F) = c". P(0) holds with F = ∅. If P(c) holds, then step 2 gives c ≤ A/((r/2)ⁿ·b), hence c ≤ N (Nat.le_floor). Let c₀ := Nat.findGreatest P N. Then P(c₀) holds (Nat.findGreatest_spec, using P(0)). Fix a finite r-separated F ⊆ K with card(F) = c₀. Moreover, P(c₀ + 1) fails. If c₀ + 1 ≤ N, this is Nat.findGreatest_is_greatest. If c₀ + 1 > N, it follows from the bound c ≤ N.
4. Covering. Let a ∈ K, and suppose dist(a, x) > r for every x ∈ F. Then a ∉ F, since dist(a, a) = 0 < r. So F ∪ {a} is a finite r-separated subset of K (Set.pairwise_insert) with card c₀ + 1, i.e. P(c₀ + 1) holds, contradicting step 3. Hence dist(a, x) ≤ r for some x ∈ F, i.e. a ∈ B̄(x, r). So K ⊆ ⋃_{x∈F} B̄(x, r).
5. Counting. By step 2, card(F)·rⁿ = 2ⁿ·(card(F)·(r/2)ⁿ) ≤ 2ⁿ·A/b = C.
6. Take s := F. Then s ⊆ K, K ⊆ ⋃_{x∈s} B̄(x, r) and card(s)·rⁿ ≤ C. The constant C was fixed in step 1 before r was chosen, so it works for every r ∈ (0, 1].
key_steps: U := thickening(1, K) has finite volume A; b := Lⁿ(B(0,1)) > 0; C := 2ⁿA/b.
A finite r-separated F ⊆ K satisfies card(F)·(r/2)ⁿ·b ≤ A, since the disjoint balls B(x, r/2) lie in U.
Choose an r-separated finite F ⊆ K of maximal cardinality (Nat.findGreatest; cardinalities ≤ ⌊A/((r/2)ⁿb)⌋).
